newsitem.title: USA: "Victor/Victoria" co-star sick over Liza's flub - Post.
newsitem.headline: "Victor/Victoria" co-star sick over Liza's flub - Post.

text.p: Broadway's "Victor/Victoria" co-star Tony Roberts has thrown a "hissy fit" over Liza Minnelli's alleged inability to deliver her lines and was out sick until Julie Andrews returns to the show, the New York Post said on Sunday.
The tabloid quoted unnamed sources as saying Roberts, 57, blew his stack after Minnelli flubbed her lines during last Wednesday's matinee.
"Liza has a line that is supposed to be, 'I'm a second-rate hoofer,' but instead she said 'I'm a second-rate hooker,'" the source said.
Minnelli, 50, has been filling in as Andrews' vacation replacement since Jan. 7 and mostly selling out the run. Andrews was due back Feb. 4.
"Mr. Roberts is out of the show with the flu bug and will hopefully be back next week," the paper quoted the show's publicist as saying.
The unidentified source also told the Post that Roberts called the producers after the show last week and said, "You can't expect me to do my job if she can't do hers."
Roberts' understudy has been filling in since, the newspaper said.
Minnelli's spokesman, Lee Solters, denied there were any problems between the two co-stars and told the Post: "This is just the work of back-biters spreading rumours and gossip."
And Minnelli told a local radio station that Roberts actually thought her flub was funny.
The musical, based on the hit 1982 film of the same name which also starred Andrews, is about a woman in 1930s Paris who pretends to be a female impersonator, or drag queen.
